android.desc: Starting in November 2025, CalcNote transitioned to an in-app subscription model. All features of CalcNote Pro are now available through in-app purchases in the free version of CalcNote. If you have already purchased CalcNote Pro, you do not need to pay again. You can continue using CalcNote Pro permanently with no additional cost. In other words, CalcNote Pro will continue to be maintained as a lifetime-license edition alongside the free version. For this reason, CalcNote Pro is priced very high. New users are strongly encouraged to use the subscription offered through the free version instead of purchasing this Pro edition. CalcNote is a revolutionary calculator app designed for smartphones. It allows you to jot down calculations in a notepad-like interface, and the results are computed and displayed instantly—eliminating the need for pressing the equal button. You can write multiple calculations at once, enabling you to see numerous problems and their answers simultaneously. Adjustments to any part of your calculations are possible at any time without the need to start over; simply correct the mistaken part, and a recalculation occurs automatically. Merging the advanced functionalities of spreadsheet software with the convenience of a calculator, CalcNote represents the next generation of calculator apps, making it a must-have tool for quick and efficient calculations. [A Fusion of Calculator and Notepad] With CalcNote, you can input calculations as if you're writing a note, and computations are performed automatically. Calculations are always displayed, making it easy to spot any mistakes. Furthermore, you can jot down notes alongside your calculations, enabling you to compute text-mixed expressions like the examples below: Example: Shop A USD 18 * 2 items + USD 4 (shipping) Shop B USD 19 * 2 items (free shipping) + 8% (sales tax) Shop C USD 18.30 * 2 items + USD 5 (shipping) - USD 2 (point redemption) By keeping calculations and notes together, the purpose of your computations becomes clear at a glance when reviewing them later. Calculations and results can be saved as files, printed, or sent via email using Android's share function. quotes.text:
I haven't seen Soulver, but it looks very similiar to the one I use on Mac, called Numi. On Android, I use an app called CalcNote which works in a similiar way. Neither does graphing, but you can do common formulas and functions like cos/sin/rad. I use numi for simple calculations, and find it fantastic when I'm trying to figure out project stuff. A recent use is entering wall dimensions to  figure out square footage and compare different building materials. I often leave most of my old calculations in numi like a long-lived numerical memory.

https://numi.app/
